Abstract.AbstractText: The objective of the presented work was to formulate and investigate the rheological behavior of non-aqueous gels containing 0.5% of meloxicam (MLX) in a non-ionic, dissolved form. Fumed silica and SynperonicTM PE/L 62 were used as structure forming components. Arlasolve®, Transcutol®, ethanol and DMSO were applied as solubilizers and potential skin absorption enhancers. In the first step, the preformulation studies were conducted in order to optimize the composition of the vehicle. The main acceptance criterion was the ability of the medium to dissolve MLX, which was confirmed by the lack of drug crystals and proper clarity of the formulation. Three formulations were selected for further investigation. Simultaneously three placebo samples, without MLX, were tested. Evaluation of the rheological parameters was performed on rotational rheometer. The samples were tested with the titanium plate-plate geometry (Ф 35 mm). The measuring gap was set at 1.0 mm. The temperature was set at 32.0±0.2oC. Evaluation of the rheological parameters included plotting of the flow curves in a controlled rate and stress mode and the advanced oscillatory assay. The obtained data were used for calculation of the yield points and structure recovery. The gels were also examined in terms of spreadability and loss of volatile components.
